receipt.summary: PASS. Independent read-only acceptance of the per-symbol protection change found no permission widening. KisGateway.reconcile resets verified_symbols/entry_reconciled before any work (fail-closed on mid-reconcile exceptions), builds verified_symbols only from local positions whose broker holding quantity matches exactly, and requires local==remote for entry_reconciled — so entries can never open while any attributed position is unprotected. Because the new regression test stubs gateway.submit, I independently exercised the submit-level gates offline with the existing fake KIS client: an unverified symbol sell is rejected with position_reconciliation_required, a buy under unattributed remote exposure is rejected with entry_reconciliation_required, and a matched symbol whose orderable quantity was consumed by an external working order is rejected with broker_sell_quantity_unavailable — zero broker order calls in all three. Required verification passed (33 passed, exit 0) and the full offline suite passed (1474 passed / 2 skipped, exit 0), matching 1471 + 3 new regressions. No edits, no writes to the repo working tree, no network/broker/Slack/AI/Docker calls, no subdelegation. Five low, non-blocking findings remain: the submit-level permission gates have no automated coverage; the stranded symbol is not named in the human-facing report or Slack alert; seven dead imports remain in quantpilot/paper; SANDBOX_OUTPUT_LIMIT is unreachable with the production bounded_run; and the unsupported_subprocess_options guard and known_order_state_changed label are untested.

criteria.criterion: Independent acceptance of per-symbol protection without enabling unsafe orders
criteria.evidence: broker.py:113-114 resets verified_symbols/entry_reconciled before any reconcile work, so a mid-reconcile exception (verify_cash raising experiment_cash_ledger_mismatch, or get_cancelable_orders failing) leaves both fail-closed. broker.py:146-150 builds verified_symbols only from local.items() with remote.get(symbol)==quantity, so it can never contain a symbol the local ledger does not hold. broker.py:198-202 requires local==remote for entry_reconciled; since every local position quantity is >0, an unverified symbol implies local!=remote, hence entries are always blocked whenever any position is unprotected (verified by probe 1: verified=['005930'] while entry path stays closed). runtime.py:169-176 skips only unmatched positions and audits position_awaiting_reconciliation. Because the new test stubs gateway.submit (test_paper_review_regressions.py:210), I exercised submit directly offline: unverified-symbol sell -> position_reconciliation_required, blocked buy -> entry_reconciliation_required, matched symbol with orderable_quantity consumed by an external working order -> broker_sell_quantity_unavailable. Zero broker order calls in all three probes.

findings.evidence: test_one_quantity_divergence_does_not_strand_another_position replaces the real gateway with `gateway.submit = lambda order, *args: submitted.append(order)`, so it proves only the runtime-side skip. A repo-wide grep for position_reconciliation_required and entry_reconciliation_required returns hits in quantpilot/paper/broker.py:218,220 only — no test anywhere asserts either rejection. I confirmed both gates work today by running them offline (probe 1 and probe 2, zero broker order calls), but nothing in the suite would fail if a future refactor dropped the second layer of defense on this critical-risk permission path.
findings.proposal: Add two small tests against the real KisGateway.submit (no stub): a sell for an unverified symbol must raise position_reconciliation_required, and a buy while entry_reconciled is False must raise entry_reconciliation_required, both asserting client.order_calls == 0. The offline scenarios I ran translate directly into test bodies using the existing Client fixture from test_intraday_durable_gateway.

findings.evidence: reconcile persists store.put('unverified_symbols', ...) (broker.py:151) and snapshot() exposes it (reporting.py:75), but render() never prints it, and runtime.alert() enqueues only 'QuantPilot 모의운용 알림: {code}' with the reason code (runtime.py:42-46). Before this change a single mismatch blocked the whole cycle, which was loud; now the system keeps running with exactly one position unprotected and the only symbol-level trace is the position_awaiting_reconciliation audit row plus `status --json`. The operator reading the Slack report sees 상태 account_exposure_unattributed and cannot tell which holding lost its stop.
findings.proposal: In render(), when report['unverified_symbols'] is non-empty, append a line naming those symbols (e.g. '보호 대기: 000660 — 브로커 수량 불일치'), and include the symbol list in the alert payload enqueued for account_exposure_unattributed.

findings.evidence: An AST scan plus grep confirmation shows seven unused imports still in the paper module: broker.py:7 OPEN (only TERMINAL is used), runtime.py:6 asdict, runtime.py:8 math, runtime.py:13 OPEN, cli.py:8 sys, calendar.py:4 timedelta, reporting.py:4 timezone. Each name appears exactly once in its file — on its own import line. The reported 'removed dead import' fix was a single-site removal, not a sweep.
findings.proposal: Drop the seven names listed above. All are stdlib or intra-package imports with no side effects, so removal is behaviour-preserving; the full suite (1474 passed) covers every affected module.

findings.evidence: run_signal_code passes max_output_bytes=config.max_output_bytes to bounded_run whenever subprocess_runner is None (lab.py:898-902), so in production bounded_run raises ValueError('subprocess_output_limit') (process.py:56-57) before control ever reaches the len(stdout) > config.max_output_bytes branch. That ValueError falls through to the catch-all at lab.py:937 and is reported as MALFORMED_OUTPUT. test_signal_runner_bounds_time_and_output (test_paper_strategy_lab.py:388-394) only reaches SANDBOX_OUTPUT_LIMIT through an injected runner that returns oversized bytes, so the assertion does not describe production behaviour. Both paths are fail-closed and neither can emit an order, so this is diagnostics only.
findings.proposal: Catch the bounded_run limit explicitly — e.g. `except ValueError as exc: return LabError(code=LabErrorCode.SANDBOX_OUTPUT_LIMIT if str(exc) == 'subprocess_output_limit' else LabErrorCode.MALFORMED_OUTPUT)` before the generic handler — so the recorded lab error code matches the real cause.

findings.evidence: test_paper_process_bounds.py covers only the output budget and the timeout kill; nothing exercises the new `if not capture_output or text or shell: raise ValueError('unsupported_subprocess_options')` guard. Likewise, no test asserts the new reconciliation_reason value 'known_order_state_changed' (broker.py:184) — a grep for that string finds it only in broker.py. Neither affects order permission (both branches still set unmanaged=True and block entries), so this is coverage debt rather than a defect.
findings.proposal: Add one parametrised assertion that bounded_run(..., text=True) / shell=True / capture_output=False raises unsupported_subprocess_options, and one reconcile test where every unmatched cancelable row matches a known dispatch by order number, branch, symbol, side and quantity, asserting reason == 'known_order_state_changed' and entry_reconciled is False.

unresolvedRisks: The per-symbol design deliberately allows a protective sell on a matched symbol while an unmanaged external working order exists on the account. Safety then rests entirely on the broker-reported orderable_quantity check in submit (broker.py:225-230), which I confirmed rejects the over-sell offline. If a real KIS paper balance ever reports orderable_quantity without deducting a pending external sell, that single check is the only thing between a matched symbol and a double sell. Worst case remains a broker rejection (Korean cash accounts cannot go short), not a short position.

Broker-side timing skew between get_daily_orders_and_fills and get_balance can transiently make a genuinely correct position unverified, suspending its stop-loss for that cycle. This is fail-closed and always accompanied by an incident alert (an unverified symbol necessarily makes local != remote, hence entry_reconciled False), but it is an availability cost of the change that only live paper running will quantify.
